# pip-bootstrap-lock.txt
#
# Hash-pinned constraints for the pip/setuptools/wheel INSTALLER TOOLCHAIN
# itself (011.013-T, resolves AFE0E95C), installed BEFORE
# .github/constraints/autoharness-lock.txt in the `topology-check` job
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml). autoharness-lock.txt pins autoharness and its
# full transitive closure, but the installer tools that PERFORM that
# install (pip, setuptools, wheel) and the Python patch version were, until
# this unit, ambient on the runner -- unpinned and unverified.
#
# BOOTSTRAP ORDERING (load-bearing): this file's packages are installed
# FIRST, with `--require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps` from THIS
# lock file alone, using the runner's preinstalled pip. Only after that
# succeeds does the autoharness-lock.txt install run. If the ordering were
# reversed, the hardened installer would not be the one PERFORMING the
# hardened install -- it would already be too late.
#
# TRUST ROOT (stated explicitly, per 011.013-T): pinning pip using the
# runner's own preinstalled pip is irreducibly trust-on-first-use (TOFU).
# This file closes the gap for every subsequent install in the job (this
# one, and autoharness's), but the very first invocation of the runner's
# ambient pip to fetch these hash-pinned wheels is not itself covered by
# any prior verification -- there is no lower turtle. This is a documented,
# accepted boundary, not a silent gap.
#
# PYTHON PIN COUPLING (load-bearing, recorded next to both pins): every
# hash below was resolved for cp312 / manylinux_2_17_x86_64 (Python 3.12,
# the exact version this job's `actions/setup-python` step pins). The
# `setup-python` version pin MUST stay within 3.12 for these hashes to
# remain satisfiable -- bumping Python without re-resolving this file
# breaks the install with a hash mismatch (fail-closed, not silently
# wrong).
#
# RESOLUTION PROVENANCE: versions/hashes below were resolved on 2026-09-06
# directly from the public PyPI JSON API (https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json
# and https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json), never a local
# index/proxy -- see docs/compound/2026-09-05-pip-index-proxy-staleness-vs-
# real-ci.md for why a corporate/local proxy's view of "latest" cannot be
# trusted to match what the public CI runner will actually fetch. Only the
# `py3-none-any` wheel digest is pinned for each package (matching
# --only-binary=:all:); no sdist is listed, which additionally forecloses
# the unhashed-sdist PEP 517 build-isolation fallback path.
#
# MAINTENANCE: version bumps are deliberate, not automatic. To bump, repeat
# the direct-PyPI-JSON-API resolution above for the new target version, and
# never hand-edit a hash.

pip==26.2.1 \
    --hash=sha256:71138adf1f4ca900cdb7d289c21b7494329f2332b6d85f0e1c42108c0384ed3e
setuptools==84.0.0 \
    --hash=sha256:51a52592b3b99e102b609654876bd65f19f999935166d1352678931132b0c670
wheel==0.48.0 \
    --hash=sha256:3217dcc807155e45db462d7ef2431f5ddda0d7273b700d05a67b271ceb1287ab
